historical_names.notes: Western Han established Lexiang County (乐乡县), merged into Yongning in Northern Qi before Sui adopted Qingyuan in 598 CE.

historical_names.name: Yongning
historical_names.source: Book of Han (Han Shu, Geography Treatise, 2 CE)
historical_names.notes: Western Han established Lexiang County (乐乡县), merged into Yongning in Northern Qi before Sui adopted Qingyuan in 598 CE.

b_huairong.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Huairong County (怀戎县), established by Northern Qi (550–577 CE; terminus ante quem 577 CE) and later seat of Tang Guizhou (妫州) in 634 CE (Zhenguan 8), recorded in the Book of Sui and Old Book of Tang.
b_huairong.etymology_analysis: A frontier pacification name meaning 'conciliating the Rong (steppe peoples),' established by Northern Qi and serving as the seat of Tang Guizhou.

historical_names.name: Pan
historical_names.source: Book of Han (Han Shu, Geography Treatise, 2 CE)
historical_names.notes: Qin and Han Shanggu Commandery governed Juyang (沮阳) and Pan (潘) counties in this area prior to Northern Qi establishing Huairong.

historical_names.name: Juyang
historical_names.source: Book of Han (Han Shu, Geography Treatise, 2 CE)
historical_names.notes: Qin and Han Shanggu Commandery governed Juyang (沮阳) and Pan (潘) counties in this area prior to Northern Qi establishing Huairong.

b_jinshan_2.first_mention_attestation: First dated attestation in 886 CE (Tang Guangqi 2), when Youzhou Jiedushi Li Kuangwei petitioned to establish Ruzhou (儒州) with its seat at Jinshan County (缙山县), as recorded in Ruzhou historical records.

natural_proper_name.name: Jinyun Mountain / Jinshan (缙云山 / 缙山)

b_jinshan_2.etymology_analysis: Named after Jinyun Mountain (缙云山, also called Jinshan 缙山); in the late Tang (886 CE), Guichuan County was renamed Jinshan County and made the seat of Ruzhou.

historical_names.name: Guichuan
historical_names.source: Yanqing District Wikipedia / Tang administrative records (624 CE)
historical_names.notes: Established in 624 CE (Tang Wude 7) as Guichuan County (妫川县, named after the Gui River) under Guizhou before being renamed Jinshan in the late Tang.

b_yuyang.first_mention_attestation: Established as Yuyang Commandery (渔阳郡) and Yuyang County (渔阳县) in the Warring States period (Yan) and standardized among the Qin Empire's 36 commanderies in 221 BCE, recorded in Shiji and Book of Han.

morphemes.translation: north bank of a river / sunny side

b_yuyang.etymology_analysis: A locator compound meaning 'north of the Yu River' (渔水之阳, modern Baihe). Originally located in Miyun/Huairou under Yan and Qin, the name was later transferred to Wuzhong (modern Jizhou, Tianjin) under the Tang Dynasty.

b_sanhe.first_mention_attestation: Established as Sanhe County (三河县) in 716 CE (Tang Kaiyuan 4) from the eastern part of Lu County, as recorded in the Old Book of Tang and New Book of Tang.

natural_proper_name.name: Three Rivers (Ju, Ru, and Baoqiu Rivers / 泃河、洳河、鲍邱河)

b_sanhe.etymology_analysis: Named 'Three Rivers' because the county sits near the confluence of three waterways (traditionally identified as the Ju, Ru/Qidu, and Baoqiu rivers).

historical_names.name: Linju
historical_names.source: Sanhe County (Hebei) Wikipedia / Book of Later Han
historical_names.notes: Part of Lu County (潞县) from 26 CE; briefly split off as Linju County (临泃县) from 619 to 627 CE before being re-established as Sanhe in 716 CE.

historical_names.name: Lu
historical_names.source: Sanhe County (Hebei) Wikipedia / Book of Later Han
historical_names.notes: Part of Lu County (潞县) from 26 CE; briefly split off as Linju County (临泃县) from 619 to 627 CE before being re-established as Sanhe in 716 CE.

b_wuqing.first_mention_attestation: Renamed Wuqing County (武清县) in 742 CE (Tang Tianbao 1) from Yongnu County, as recorded in the Old Book of Tang and New Book of Tang.
b_wuqing.etymology_analysis: An imperial renaming in 742 CE meaning 'pacified through martial prowess' (以武功廓清之义), replacing the older name Yongnu.

historical_names.name: Yongnu
historical_names.source: Wuqing District Wikipedia / Book of Han (Han Shu)
historical_names.notes: Western Han established Quanzhou and Yongnu counties in 106 BCE; Northern Wei merged Quanzhou into Yongnu in 448 CE before Tang renamed it Wuqing in 742 CE.

historical_names.name: Quanzhou
historical_names.source: Wuqing District Wikipedia / Book of Han (Han Shu)
historical_names.notes: Western Han established Quanzhou and Yongnu counties in 106 BCE; Northern Wei merged Quanzhou into Yongnu in 448 CE before Tang renamed it Wuqing in 742 CE.

b_zunhua.first_mention_attestation: Established as Zunhua County (遵化县) during the Later Tang Dynasty (923–936 CE; exact year unrecorded, terminus ante quem 936 CE) on the site of Pingzhou's Horse-Purchasing Office (买马监) under Jizhou.
b_zunhua.etymology_analysis: An auspicious administrative name meaning 'following civilizing transformation' (遵循教化), coined when Later Tang elevated the Pingzhou Horse-Purchasing Office to a county in 923–936 CE.

historical_names.name: Wuzhong
historical_names.source: Book of Han (Han Shu, Geography Treatise, 2 CE)
historical_names.notes: Historically part of Right Beiping Commandery (Wuzhong County in Han); later the Tang Pingzhou Horse-Purchasing Office (买马监) occupied the site prior to Later Tang establishing Zunhua County.

b_lulong.first_mention_attestation: Renamed Lulong County (卢龙县) in 598 CE (Sui Kaihuang 18) from Xinchang County, as recorded in the Book of Sui (Sui Shu, Geography Treatise).
b_lulong.etymology_analysis: Named after the ancient Lulong Pass (卢龙塞) in the Yan Mountains, a strategic defile north of Pingzhou.

historical_names.name: Feiru
historical_names.source: Book of Han (Han Shu, Geography Treatise, 2 CE)
historical_names.notes: Western Han established Feiru County (肥如县); Northern Wei split off Xinchang County (新昌县), which Sui renamed Lulong in 598 CE.

historical_names.name: Xinchang
historical_names.source: Book of Han (Han Shu, Geography Treatise, 2 CE)
historical_names.notes: Western Han established Feiru County (肥如县); Northern Wei split off Xinchang County (新昌县), which Sui renamed Lulong in 598 CE.

b_anxi_2.first_mention_attestation: Established as Anxi County (安喜县) in Pingzhou in 923 CE (Liao Tianzan 2), when Liao Taizu resettled captives from Dingzhou's Anxi County at modern Qian'an, recorded in Qian'an history and Liao Shi.
b_anxi_2.etymology_analysis: A transplanted Liao Dynasty county in Pingzhou (distinct from the older Han/Tang Anxi County in Dingzhou), named in 923 CE after the captive population brought from Dingzhou's Anxi County; renamed Qian'an in 1167 CE.

historical_names.name: Lingzhi
historical_names.source: Book of Han (Han Shu, Geography Treatise, 2 CE)
historical_names.notes: In Han times the area was Lingzhi County (令支县) under Liaoxi Commandery, and under Tang it was part of Lulong County in Pingzhou.

historical_names.name: Lulong
historical_names.source: Book of Han (Han Shu, Geography Treatise, 2 CE)
historical_names.notes: In Han times the area was Lingzhi County (令支县) under Liaoxi Commandery, and under Tang it was part of Lulong County in Pingzhou.

b_macheng_2.first_mention_attestation: Established as Macheng County (马城县) under Pingzhou in 740 CE (Tang Kaiyuan 28), as recorded in the New Book of Tang and Pingzhou administrative tables.
b_macheng_2.etymology_analysis: Established in 740 CE under Tang Pingzhou (Beiping Commandery) in eastern Hebei (modern Laoting/Luannan area).

b_shicheng_2.first_mention_attestation: Established as Shicheng County (石城县) under Pingzhou in 697 CE (Wu Zhou Wansuitongtian 2) when Linyu County was abolished, recorded in the New Book of Tang and Pingzhou administrative tables (an earlier Shicheng 石成 existed in Western Han Right Beiping).
b_shicheng_2.etymology_analysis: Literally 'Stone Citadel,' established in 697 CE under Pingzhou (modern Fengrun, Tangshan), reviving the name of an earlier Han-era county in Right Beiping.

historical_names.name: Linyu
historical_names.source: Book of Han (漢書·地理志, 2 CE) and New Book of Tang (新唐書·地理志)
historical_names.notes: Linyu County (臨渝縣, attested since Western Han and restored under Tang in 641 CE) was abolished in 697 CE when Shicheng County was established.

b_miyun.first_mention_attestation: Established as Miyun Commandery and Miyun County (密云县) in 397 CE (Northern Wei Huangshi 2), as recorded in the Book of Wei (Wei Shu, Geography Treatise).
b_miyun.etymology_analysis: Named after Mount Miyun (密云山, 'Dense Cloud Mountain'), so called because thick clouds gather on its peaks before rain.

historical_names.name: Baitan
historical_names.source: Miyun District Wikipedia / Book of Han
historical_names.notes: Part of Qin Yuyang Commandery (221 BCE) and Han Baitan County (白檀县, 2 CE) prior to Northern Wei establishing Miyun in 397 CE.

historical_names.name: Yuyang
historical_names.source: Miyun District Wikipedia / Book of Han
historical_names.notes: Part of Qin Yuyang Commandery (221 BCE) and Han Baitan County (白檀县, 2 CE) prior to Northern Wei establishing Miyun in 397 CE.

b_yanle.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Yanle County (燕乐县), seat of Anle Commandery in the Book of Wei (Wei Shu, Geography Treatise, completed 554 CE), which dates its establishment to Northern Wei (Yanhe/Taiping Zhenjun era, 430s–440s CE); later seat of Sui Tanzhou in 596 CE.
b_yanle.etymology_analysis: Established by Northern Wei as the seat of Anle Commandery (安乐郡), pairing the regional name Yan (燕) with 'joy/peace' (乐), and serving as the initial seat of Sui Tanzhou until 693 CE.

b_huairou.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Huairou County (怀柔县), seat of Tang Thanhan Prefecture (弹汗州, later Guishun Prefecture 归顺州) established in 648 CE (Zhenguan 22) in modern Shunyi, recorded in Tang administrative histories.
b_huairou.etymology_analysis: A classical Tang pacification name meaning 'to draw near and conciliate' (怀柔), first used for the Khitan-settled county under Tang Thanhan/Guishun Prefecture in 648 CE.

b_xingtang.first_mention_attestation: Established as Xingtang County (行唐县) in Tanzhou by Liao Taizu (r. 907–926 CE; c. 921–923 CE campaigns against Dingzhou), who resettled captives from Dingzhou's Xingtang County onto open land in Tanzhou, recorded in the History of Liao (Liao Shi, vol. 40).

morphemes.translation: Tang (ancient state/place name, from original Xingtang in Hebei)

b_xingtang.etymology_analysis: A transplanted Liao Dynasty county in Tanzhou (distinct from the ancient Warring States/Northern Wei Xingtang County near Shijiazhuang), named in the 920s CE after the captive population relocated from Dingzhou's Xingtang County.

b_ji.first_mention_attestation: Attested from c. 1045 BCE (early Western Zhou enfeoffment of the State of Ji 蓟国) and as the capital of Yan (蓟城) in the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, recorded in Shiji.
b_ji.etymology_analysis: Named after the thistle plant (蓟) abundant in the region; served as the capital of ancient Ji and Yan, and later as the seat of Youzhou (幽州) through the Tang Dynasty.

b_lu.first_mention_attestation: Renamed Lu County (潞县) in 26 CE (Eastern Han Jianwu 2) from Western Han Lu County (路县), recorded in the Book of Later Han and Tongzhou District histories.
b_lu.etymology_analysis: Eastern Han added the water radical 氵 to the older Western Han name 路 (Lu) in 26 CE, reflecting its location along the Lu River (潞水, modern North Canal/Chaobai system).

b_changping.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Changping County (昌平县) under Shanggu Commandery in the Book of Han (Han Shu, Geography Treatise, 2 CE).
b_changping.etymology_analysis: An auspicious Han-era placename meaning 'prosperous and peaceful,' attested in the Book of Han under Shanggu Commandery.

b_anci.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Anci County (安次县) under Bohai Commandery in the Book of Han (Han Shu, Geography Treatise, 2 CE).
b_anci.etymology_analysis: Established in the Western Han Dynasty under Bohai Commandery (later transferred to Guangyang Commandery and Tang Youzhou), meaning 'peaceful staging post.'

b_yongqing_2.first_mention_attestation: Renamed Yongqing County (永清县) in 742 CE (Tang Tianbao 1) from Huichang County under Youzhou (Fanyang Commandery), recorded in the Old Book of Tang and New Book of Tang.
b_yongqing_2.etymology_analysis: An imperial renaming in 742 CE meaning 'eternally pacified/clear,' replacing the earlier Tang name Huichang.

historical_names.name: Wulong
historical_names.source: Youzhou (Ancient) Wikipedia / Old Book of Tang
historical_names.notes: Established as Wulong County (武隆县) by splitting Anci and Gu'an, renamed Huichang County (会昌县) in 710 CE, and renamed Yongqing in 742 CE.

historical_names.name: Huichang
historical_names.source: Youzhou (Ancient) Wikipedia / Old Book of Tang
historical_names.notes: Established as Wulong County (武隆县) by splitting Anci and Gu'an, renamed Huichang County (会昌县) in 710 CE, and renamed Yongqing in 742 CE.

b_fanyang.first_mention_attestation: Established as Fanyang County (范阳县) in 226 BCE (21st year of King Zheng of Qin), recorded in the Book of Han and historical gazetteers; in 624 CE Tang renamed Zhuo County to Fanyang County.

morphemes.translation: north bank of a river / sunny side

b_fanyang.etymology_analysis: A locator compound meaning 'north of the Fan River' (范水之北), originally established by Qin in 226 BCE in Dingxing and transferred to Zhuo County (modern Zhuozhou) in 624 CE.

b_guan.first_mention_attestation: Renamed Gu'an County (固安县) in 589 CE (Sui Kaihuang 9) from Fangcheng County under Youzhou, recorded in the Book of Sui (Sui Shu).
b_guan.etymology_analysis: An auspicious administrative name meaning 'firm and pacified,' adopted by the Sui Dynasty in 589 CE when renaming the Western Han Fangcheng County.

historical_names.name: Fangcheng
historical_names.source: Gu'an County Wikipedia / Book of Han (Han Shu, 2 CE)
historical_names.notes: Western Han established Fangcheng County (方城县), which retained that name until Sui renamed it Gu'an in 589 CE.
